scenario: A new user in a current workspace
prompt: I just installed PKA. How do I use this?
expect: checks the workspace with tool calls before teaching: looks for .pka/ and CLAUDE.md and runs the plugin's `pka-tools status --workspace … --json` and `upgrade-roles.py --workspace … --dry-run`; treats the workspace as bootstrapped and current, suggesting no upgrade; offers the full tour, described as eleven short modules taking about 30 minutes, or a jump to a specific topic; teaches by describing prompts the user can try, and moves, creates or edits no file apart from its own session-log entry

scenario: The tour, one module at a time
prompt: Give me a tour of PKA.
expect: starts with orientation: what PKA is, the Repo Map, roles, the session log; its examples use this workspace's own folder names from the Repo Map (for example knowledge/leadership/ or knowledge/personnel/); ends the module with concrete prompts to try; checks in with the user before the next module instead of delivering every module in one reply; the second reply covers finding things; where it describes the scope of the tour it includes topic wikis, health checks, people and timelines, and the pointer layer (eleven modules); moves, creates or edits no file apart from its own session-log entry

prompt: How do I capture meeting notes?
expect: answers with the meeting-capture module only, not the whole tour; explains the three modes: live capture, reconcile against a transcript, route only; checks whether take-notes and resolve-against-transcript are available and says that without thinkkit only route-only works here; tells the user what to say to pka-meetings to do it, and neither captures nor files anything itself

prompt: How do I find things in my knowledge base?
expect: answers with the finding-things module only; explains the four kinds of query: simple lookup, cross-repo search, project snapshot, date-scoped; its example prompts use this workspace's folder or person names; ends with prompts to try

scenario: The menu, in a workspace first set up on the installed release
expect: gives a menu of capabilities with a short description of each; asks which one to go into; does not launch the full tour unprompted; offers no `what's new` item (the workspace was first set up on this release: there is no .pka/upgrade-backups/); suggests no upgrade

scenario: A folder where PKA was never set up
prompt: Walk me through PKA — I'm new.
expect: checks for .pka/ and CLAUDE.md before teaching; says PKA is not set up in this folder yet; offers to hand off to pka-bootstrap, with the tour to follow; does not start the bootstrap itself: no file is created

prompt: How do I drop files into the system?
expect: answers with the inbox module only; explains team-inbox/ as the input queue and owner-inbox/ as where outputs are delivered; explains that transcripts are held for pka-meetings instead of being routed; explains batch processing with grouped routing proposals; moves and creates no file apart from its own session-log entry

scenario: A workspace bootstrapped before v1.7.0: no manifest, no toolkit
prompt: Give me a tour of PKA.
expect: runs the plugin's copy of `pka-tools status --workspace <root> --json`; runs no `.pka/bin/pka-tools` command (there is none); says, before starting any module, that the workspace is behind the installed release (set up before v1.7.0, installed {{plugin_version}}); offers to walk through the upgrade first; changes no file

scenario: The upgrade walkthrough previews and hands off
prompt: Give me a tour of PKA.
followups: Yes, walk me through the upgrade.
expect: runs the plugin's `pka-tools install --workspace <root> --dry-run` and explains its result in plain language (what would be installed, updated or kept); describes the three things `bootstrap upgrade` does, in order: the toolkit and helper scripts, the index migration (it asks first and the database is backed up), the role files (backed up, sections added, the user's own not rewritten); says nothing is committed; says the upgrade needs Python 3.9 or newer; ends by telling the user to say `bootstrap upgrade`; never runs the installer without --dry-run, `db migrate --apply`, or upgrade-roles.py without --dry-run; no file in the workspace has changed when the run ends

scenario: After the upgrade has run in this session
expect: after the last message it runs both checks again (the plugin's `pka-tools status … --json` and `upgrade-roles.py … --dry-run`) and confirms that the workspace is current; explains the upgrade's summary: where the backups are (.pka/upgrade-backups/) and that the changes are the user's to review; teaches what is new since the release the workspace was on as things the user can now do, with one prompt to try for each; those prompts use this workspace's folder or person names; logs a session-log entry whose summary begins `What's new in v{{plugin_version}}`

scenario: A current workspace that was upgraded at some point and has not seen what's new

text: (the roster as it was before the upgrade)

expect: suggests no upgrade (the workspace is current); lists `what's new in v{{plugin_version}}` first in its menu of topics; does not start the what's-new walkthrough unprompted

scenario: One how-do-I question in a workspace that is behind
prompt: How do I capture meeting notes?
expect: says in one sentence that the workspace is behind the installed release and that the upgrade walkthrough is available afterwards; then answers with the meeting-capture module; flags the parts of the answer that depend on the upgrade; does not put the upgrade walkthrough before the answer

scenario: The user declines the upgrade offer and takes the tour
followups: Not now, just give me the tour.
expect: after `not now` it continues with the tour; names what depends on the upgrade as it comes up; does not raise the upgrade again after it was declined; the closing session-log entry has `bootstrap upgrade not run` in its open-threads field; runs no installer without --dry-run, no migration and no role upgrade

scenario: The workspace's manifest records a newer release than the installed plugin
expect: says the installed plugin ({{plugin_version}}) is older than the release the workspace was upgraded on (99.0.0) and should be updated; does not suggest `bootstrap upgrade`; then carries on as for a returning user, offering topics or the tour

scenario: The toolkit is current because the librarian installed it, but `bootstrap upgrade` never ran
expect: runs the plugin's `upgrade-roles.py --workspace <root> --dry-run`; treats the workspace as behind although the toolkit versions are equal; says the toolkit is current and the role files are not; offers the upgrade walkthrough before the tour

scenario: Toolkit and roles current, index on an older schema
expect: says the index was not migrated, so search and indexing are off; says that `bootstrap upgrade` offers the migration again; runs no `install --dry-run` preview and gives no upgrade walkthrough; then offers the returning-user menu or the tour; runs no `db migrate`

scenario: 'Go ahead' after the preview is the request for the upgrade
expect: the first reply is the upgrade walkthrough: it says the workspace is behind and previews with the plugin's `install --workspace <root> --dry-run`; treats `go ahead` as the request for bootstrap upgrade and says it is switching to pka-bootstrap; then follows the upgrade procedure: runs the plugin's installer for real, then `.pka/upgrade-roles.py --workspace`; asks before running --refresh
